summary.text: Madeleine Dean is the Democratic incumbent for Pennsylvania's 4th District, which she has represented in the U.S. House since 2019. A former lawyer, college writing and ethics instructor and newspaper columnist, she served as an Abington Township commissioner and in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2012 to 2018 before winning her congressional seat in 2018. She serves on the House Appropriations and House Foreign Affairs committees.

paragraphs.text: Dean was born in 1959 and raised in Glenside, Pennsylvania, with five older brothers and one older sister.
She graduated from Abington High School and, at age 18, won election as a local committeeperson.
She earned a B.A. in English language and literature from La Salle University in 1981 and a J.D. from Widener University School of Law in 1984.
Dean practiced law in a small Philadelphia firm and with the Philadelphia Trial Lawyers Association, where she became executive director, and then opened a small law practice in Glenside.

From 2001 to 2011 she was a member of La Salle University's English Department, teaching writing and ethics, and she contributed columns to The Philadelphia Inquirer, the Daily News, The Patriot-News and other publications.
After studying politics and public service at the University of Pennsylvania's Fels School of Government, Dean was elected an Abington Township commissioner in 2011.
She won a special election to the Pennsylvania House of Representatives (District 153) in 2012 and served until 2018.

In the state House she founded and co-chaired the PA-SAFE Caucus, a coalition of legislators and advocates focused on gun violence, and in 2015 Gov. Tom Wolf appointed her to the Pennsylvania Commission for Women.
Dean won election to the U.S. House in 2018 for the 4th District; her official biography notes that Pennsylvania's 18-member House delegation then included no women.
In the 118th Congress she served on the Judiciary Committee, as vice chair in 2021-2022, and on the Foreign Affairs Committee.
She is in her fourth term and serves on the House Appropriations and House Foreign Affairs committees.
Her official biography says she is married to PJ Cunnane and that they have three sons and seven grandchildren.
